A design-review screenshot proves 'the FE serving :PORT looked like this THEN', never 'this is how it is NOW'. A stale FE (behind main) makes an already-fixed bug look live — this bit us live: a /v2 fortune-card capture at FE d58a6b8 showed an empty/stuck card that #110 had already fixed; the reporter (me) called it a live finding without checking the FE build (บอง + goo caught it). Fix: harness/capture-route.ts auto-records the FE build every run — detectFeBuild() = lsof :port -> serving worktree cwd -> git HEAD + commits-BEHIND origin/main, printed as '🏷️ FE build @capture: <hash> ... BEHIND origin/main' and required in evidence; CAPTURE.md adds the 'images expire — confirm FE current before trusting a capture' rule. Verify-the-instrument (neg-control): the SAME tool renders empty fortune at d58a6b8 (pre-fix) vs 'B+ 70%' at 20d3d05 (post-fix) — it reflects the FE's REAL state, does not fabricate; the recorded hash makes which-state unambiguous. Same shape as absence-vs-unchanged: a point-in-time image is not the present. gate_layer=process/evidence-integrity.

useHomeFortune latched a persistent doneRef BEFORE its async work, so React StrictMode's dev double-invoke deadlocks the loading flag: run A latches + starts the fetch, its cleanup sets alive=false, run B short-circuits on the latch, then run A's fetch resolves into `if (alive)` (false) → setFortune AND `finally { setLoading(false) }` are both skipped → loading stays true → the /v2 ScoreRingCard shows FortuneSkeleton forever (no empty-state, no error). Console/AST are blind (the code shape is a valid effect); the request DOES fire and returns 200 — the bug is the discarded result, not a missing call — so a network probe alone mis-diagnoses it as 'no fetch'. Ground-truth = the rendered card leaves the skeleton within a time budget. Fix = drop the doneRef latch; the effect is idempotent, each StrictMode invocation owns its `alive`, the surviving run resolves loading (also fixes a latent no-refetch-on-userId-change). Dev-only (prod mounts once); /api/home-fortune is an idempotent daily compute so the dev double-call is harmless. Teeth-proven live (run-fortune-hang.ts, neg-control-first vs the real testenv stack): MUTANT=restore latch → skeleton persists 15s+, pulses=1 → runner exits 1 CAUGHT; FIX → skeleton clears ~1.5s, fortune 'B+ 70%' + ธาตุ line render → PASS. gate_layer=runtime/rendered-text; local-only (needs the testenv DB stack, like e2e/auth-loop — not in ci.yml/design-verify).

The /v2 daily-fortune card's 'ควรเลี่ยง' (worst) text must be read from bazi's summaryItems BY KEY (key==='worst'), never by position. bazi /api/home forwards 5 KEYED items (best · worst · strength · element · officer); the old bestWorstText took summaryItems[last] = 'officer' ('ดูแลเอาใจใส่'), so 'ควรเลี่ยง' rendered the OPPOSITE meaning of key==='worst' ('อยู่บ้าน / คุมลูกน้อง / อยู่ในห้อง') — a daily inverted message the user read as ground truth. Fix: match by key per-field, fall back to facets-by-percent only when a keyed item is absent. gate_layer=data/normalize (pure). Teeth (home-fortune-best-worst.test.ts, neg-control-first): fix 5/5; MUTANT restore-to-[last] → 4 fail (worst='ดูแลเอาใจใส่' caught); restore → 5/5. `return response as RESPONSE_*` in constants/api/* makes tsc TRUST a hand-written (often wrong) response shape and hides drift — the same lie that ate the v2-home ธาตุ element (chinese-horoscope-get). Closed by PROVABILITY (approach ข), not prettier guesses: (A) endpoints we can hit read-only (chinese-horoscope-get) are typed from the REAL live shape — RESPONSE_CHINESE_HOROSCOPE_GET was rewritten to the verified 15 keys, DELETING the fabricated `analytic.habits_behaviors` and ADDING power/analytic.life/share_profile_url that my-destiny actually reads; (B) endpoints with side effects we refuse to fire (calculate saves a chart; compatibility burns a quota; otp/register/check-line hit LIVE 8x8 SMS / LINE — #184) return `UnverifiedApiResult` ({error?; [k]:unknown}) so callers must narrow, since we must NOT author a type we can't prove. Teeth are type-level (error paths can't be live-tested): neg-control run — revert a narrow (register `typeof result.code==='string'` → `result.code`) → tsc RED (TS2345 '{}' not assignable to SetStateAction<string>); restore → clean, so the honest type surfaces the drift. Real value found (approach ก would have hidden all of these by typing to match the wrong cast): compatibility-WORK was cast to the LOVE response type (system-wide copy-paste); api-otp-get had 2 stray horoscope imports; register `gotoResult(result.code)` had NO null-check ×2 (a real crash if Calculate errors, latent because the blind cast said `.code` always exists). tsc clean · 42/42 tests · zero `as RESPONSE_*` remain. gate_layer=type/static.

Fix: stack.sh `shadow_others` moves EVERY other `.env*` aside (backed up → *.testenv-shadowed) via a GLOB (whole-space, not a memorized list) so `.env` is the only active env; guard scans the WHOLE active set; guard now also scans NEXT_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL. #178: write_breadcrumb printed the backup path UNCONDITIONALLY, so the .env.disabled marker advertised a backup that was never made — fixed with test -f (states 'NO backup was made' when none exists). Script-only, no runtime touched. gate_layer=infra/shell.

#177 follow-up (บอง's review lens, caught before any PR-B run): in stack.sh up(), the LOCAL git-exclude for *.testenv-shadowed was written by ensure_local_ignore AFTER shadow_others had already renamed each prod .env* to that suffix — so between the rename and the exclude-write there was a window where a prod-secret file (mootech-be/.env.local carries SUPABASE_REAL_PRODUCTION_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, SUPABASE_REAL_DB_PASSWORD, RENDER_API_KEY — RLS-bypassing + infra-controlling, the strongest creds we hold) sat on disk under a git-COMMITABLE name (git check-ignore .env.local.testenv-shadowed → not-ignored, verified in all 3 repos). Normally a blink, but if stack.sh dies mid-run (post-copy guard fail → exit) AND the rollback trap fails to un-shadow, the key is left exposed to a commit. Low probability, unrecoverable if it fires. Fix: order ensure_local_ignore BEFORE shadow_others (and before write_breadcrumb) so the shadowed file is born already-ignored — window = ZERO. Design was already correct (the *SHADOW_SUFFIX pattern goes into .git/info/exclude); only the call order was swapped. Teeth (shadow-ignore-order.test.sh, run under bash 3.2, neg-control-first): Part A behavioral — shadow-first leaves .env.local.testenv-shadowed NOT git-ignored (window reproduced), ignore-first makes it ignored the instant it exists; Part B structural — asserts stack.sh calls ensure_local_ignore before shadow_others, MUTANT reorder-back → RED CAUGHT. 5/5 fixed, mutant caught. Script-only, no runtime/TS touched. gate_layer=infra/shell (secret-at-rest exposure window).

Real /v2 verified @ FE e98a82e + uncommitted zone3 working-tree (content-proof: ดวงสมพงค์ + 2 cards + 9 mascots paint on the real route, cannot exist on e98a82e's empty ServiceSection). #184: the test-env be.env used FAKE keys but still pointed OUTBOUND hosts at LIVE providers — LINE_HOST=api.line.me, SMS_8X8_HOST=sms.8x8.com, SUPABASE_PROJECT_URL=dummy.supabase.co, DIFY_API_URL=dify.example.com. An accidentally-invoked otp/sms/line/payment call would then reach the real provider (real SMS send / real charge attempt), even with a fake token — the request still LEAVES. guard.sh scanned only DB hosts, so it declared 'safe' while the outbound pipe was live (same blind-spot class as #177's DB-only scan). Fix (structure, not intent): (1) neutralize every outbound host in be.env to an RFC-2606 `.invalid` domain (DNS-guaranteed non-resolvable) so any accidental call dies at DNS — Omise/SendGrid hardcode their host in the SDK so their fake key is the neutralizer; (2) guard.sh now refuses any REAL provider host (api.line.me|8x8.com|omise.co|api.sendgrid.com|sendgrid.net) found ANYWHERE in an env file (whole-file value scan, comments stripped), fail-closed. Teeth (guard.test.sh, run under bash 3.2, neg-control-first): 18/18 — real 8x8/LINE/omise/sendgrid host → REFUSED, neutralized .invalid → allowed, a comment naming a provider → NOT false-refused; mutant drop a PROVIDER_PATTERN → real host slips → RED. Real-machine: BE booted with the neutralized be.env (Nest 'successfully started', :4000, GET / 200, TypeOrmCoreModule initialized against localhost:5433) and sms.8x8.invalid/line.invalid/dummy.supabase.invalid/dify.invalid all resolve NXDOMAIN while api.line.me still resolves (fail-closed proven WITHOUT firing any otp/payment endpoint). gate_layer=infra/shell + runtime-boot.

#177 real-machine gap (surfaced this round, never in sandbox): stack.sh shadowed the non-placed .env* only for `next` apps. The BE (mootech-be) is a `node`/NestJS app that loads ONLY .env (verified: no envFilePath in any ConfigModule.forRoot, no dotenv dep — nestjs/config default), so its prod .env.dev.local / .env.prod.local / .env.local (holding prod DB pooler + api.line.me + 8x8.com + the Supabase service-role key) were NEVER shadowed and stayed ACTIVE on disk. The #177 whole-active-set guard + #184 provider scan correctly REFUSED and the up rolled back fail-closed — but the stack could not come up. Fix (chosen over making the guard node-aware, which would just narrow the question so it passes): run shadow_others for EVERY app, not just next — so only the neutralized .env stays active (a real reduction of what's reachable, not a narrower guard) + defense-in-depth (prod service-role moved aside during test). ensure_local_ignore still runs BEFORE shadow_others for the BE dir (#119 window stays closed — verified the 3 shadowed BE files are git check-ignore'd). Why sandbox missed it: the #177/#178 sandbox had no node app carrying multiple prod .env.*.local files — clean-state tests can't answer dirty-state questions (2nd instance of that lesson this week).
